Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $36 million class fund, distributed automatically to identified members. The $3.5 million fee request would be subject to court approval, with any unawarded amount going to the class. Brightline would not be required to refrain from opposing the request. This structure delivers direct relief without a claims process or fee reversion.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that automatic payments to identified members and court review of fees are the right framework. Brightline can offer a $30 million class fund and $3 million in fees, with no clear-sailing commitment and any unawarded fees going to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s agreement on automatic payments and on directing any unawarded fees to the class. We can narrow the remaining gap by reducing our proposed class fund to $34 million and accepting your $3 million fee figure. All other terms remain as in your offer.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the movement on the class fund and agreement on the remaining terms. Brightline can move to a $32 million class fund while retaining automatic distribution, $3 million in court-approved fees, no clear sailing, and any unawarded fees going to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are close. To resolve the remaining gap, we propose a $33 million class fund, with automatic payments to identified members. We accept your other terms: $3 million in fees subject to court approval, no clear-sailing commitment, and any unawarded fees going to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline accepts your latest term sheet: a $33 million class fund with automatic distribution, $3 million in fees subject to court approval, no clear-sailing commitment, and any unawarded fees going to the class.

private_notes.private_reasoning: An automatic, nonreversionary distribution is feasible because Brightline can identify every member and charged card. I will seek a substantial class recovery that reflects litigation and certification risk, with a modest separate fee that does not affect the firm's compensation.

The opening offer is within Brightline’s $40 million authorization and has court-approval-friendly distribution and fee terms, but leaves little room below the cap. Counter at $33 million total while preserving automatic payments and avoiding fee provisions that could complicate approval.

The defense offer preserves automatic distribution and avoids fee terms that could divert money from the class. Its $30 million fund is substantial, especially given certification and trial risks, but there is room to negotiate before accepting in round 2. Counter at $34 million while leaving the other terms unchanged.
The latest proposal is within authorization and has favorable approval features, but a modest counteroffer may reduce Brightline’s total outlay while leaving time to settle.

The $32 million automatic-distribution offer is strong relative to the litigation risks. Still, three rounds remain, and the parties are only $2 million apart on the class fund. A $33 million midpoint proposal may improve class recovery without changing the agreed distribution and fee protections.

The $36 million total cash outlay is within authorization. Automatic distribution and fee terms support court approval. The remaining $1 million difference from our last offer does not justify risking a binding resolution.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The settlement resulted from arm’s-length negotiations between counsel after the motion to dismiss was resolved. Because the negotiations were confidential mediation communications, I do not disclose their exchanges. The agreed terms submitted for preliminary approval provide a $33 million class fund distributed automatically to identified members, with no claim form required. The separate $3 million fee provision is subject to court approval; Brightline has made no commitment not to oppose it, and any unawarded amount will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. In my judgment, the direct recovery is fair in light of the risks of certification and trial and the delay litigation would entail. Counsel’s compensation is fixed and does not depend on the fee award.
